newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: U.S. sees N.Korean incursion on border with South.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sees N.Korean incursion on border with South.

text.p: Five North Korean soldiers crossed into South Korea's portion of a border buffer zone on Monday in violation of a ceasefire accord, a U.S. military spokesman said.
"The soldiers crossed into the area at about 4.55 a.m. (1955 GMT Sunday) and we watched them for about one and a half hours," Jim Coles said.
"While their presence in the area is a violation of the armistice agreement, they did not do anything provocative. It's rugged territory up there and it's easy to miss the line markers," Coles said.

The armed soldiers crossed a demarcation line through the four-km (2.5 mile) deep Demilitarised Zone, which bisects the Korean peninsula under an armistice agreement that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
A South Korean defence ministry official said such incursions were not uncommon.
"We are not very concerned," he said.
The United States maintains 37,000 troops in South Korea to guard against any North Korean attack and heads a U.N.-mandated operation that monitors the ceasefire.
Last April scores of North Korean troops carrying heavy weapons crossed the demarcation line on three occasions within the sensitive border crossing area of Panmunjom.
Those violations followed a North Korean announcement it would no longer respect the terms of the armistice.

Tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang have been heightened since the defection in Beijing last month of a high-ranking North Korean official and the murder of a North Korean defector living in the South.
Ideologue Hwang Jang-yop sought asylum at a South Korean diplomatic mission in the Chinese capital on February 12 and negotiations on his fate are now underway.
Shortly after Hwang's defection, defector Lee Il-nam was shot by suspected North Korean agents near Seoul.
Despite tensions, North Korean officials attended a briefing by officials from South Korea and the United States on proposed four-way peace talks, also involving China.
The New York briefing was intended to lure Pyongyang into talks aimed at securing a peace agreement to replace the armistice.
